acceptance: the skeleton decision was made first — one is built only when the component owns an async query with a real pre-data gap; none for a purely-presentational, synchronous, cached, or already-parent-covered component
where warranted, the skeleton uses the shared Skeleton primitive — never a skeleton library, never a hand-rolled pulsing div; the primitive is created once as a primitive if absent
the skeleton is a separate <Component>Skeleton.tsx colocated in the same folder and exported from the index barrel — not inlined and not a loading branch baked inside the real component
it mirrors the real component's layout (same wrapper, box count and rough size) so content drops in without the page jumping, and the loading branch is wired at the consumer
in Storybook the skeleton is shown stacked under the real component per state, with no separate skeleton story file
